source.title_on_document: Stimulating or constraining creativity? Traditional vs. generative AI on divergent thinking in product design

paper_design_summary: 41 second-year product-design students from a single Chinese university each did three 10-minute chair-design ideation tasks in a lab: unaided, Internet-assisted (Baidu Images), and GenAI-assisted (Doubao text-to-image). Task order was counterbalanced by a systematic rotation schedule, and creative tendency (average vs. good) was a between-subjects factor. Three design experts rated the sketches for flexibility, originality, and elaboration on 5-point scales, fluency was the count of distinct ideas, and participants self-reported perceived creativity support.

studies.label: Chair-design ideation experiment (3 x 2 mixed design)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the three ideation methods (unaided, Internet-assisted, GenAI-assisted); every participant did all three. Order was counterbalanced by a systematic rotation schedule; random assignment is not stated.
assignment.quote: the sequence of the three design tasks was counterbalanced across participants using a systematic rotation schedule.

arms.name: Internet-assisted

arms.name: GenAI-assisted

outcomes.name: Elaboration of design outcomes
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Three independent design experts, blinded to condition, rated the detail, completeness and refinement of the hand-drawn chair design concepts on a 5-point scale: 1 = poor, 3 = average, 5 = excellent (p. 7, Table 1 and Section 3.4).

contrasts.reported: Means (SD) by creative-tendency group (average n = 21, good n = 20; same people in each method): Unaided average 3.44 (0.83), good 3.44 (0.69); GenAI-assisted average 3.37 (1.23), good 3.58 (1.00). No significant omnibus ideation-method effect (p > 0.05); Greenhouse-Geisser-corrected degrees of freedom were used. The exact F statistic, corrected degrees of freedom and exact p-value are not reported. No separate pairwise test is reported for this comparison.
contrasts.locator: p. 5, Section 3.1 (subgroup counts); p. 7, Table 1 and Section 3.4; p. 8, Table 2 and Section 4.1

eligibility.reason: The same 41 people were analyzed across the repeated ideation conditions (p. 5, Sections 3.1-3.2; p. 8, Section 4), below the 50-person core threshold. Task order was counterbalanced using a systematic rotation schedule; random assignment of people or order is not reported (p. 6, Section 3.3 and Figure 2). The output-scored measures are expert-rated originality, flexibility and elaboration, plus the count of distinct ideas for fluency (p. 7, Table 1 and Section 3.4). Code quasi_people and retain as observational context under creativity-codebook.md Sections 3-4 and the form-spec.md design_class field note; this document does not establish a randomized people study.

one_line_finding: Among 41 design students, GenAI-assisted ideation scores were lower for fluency, flexibility and originality than unaided or Internet-assisted scores, with no significant elaboration effect (p > 0.05; p. 8, Table 2 and Section 4.1; p. 10, Figure 4), while self-reported usability, exploration and immersion were higher than unaided, result worth effort favored Internet-assisted over GenAI-assisted (p = 0.040), and expressiveness and enjoyment had no significant method main effects (pp. 9-10, Section 4.2).
notes: The condition counts repeat the same 41 people; the average (n = 21) and good (n = 20) creative-tendency subgroups are measured groups, not independently assigned treatment arms (p. 5, Sections 3.1-3.2; p. 8, Section 4). Table 2 reports subgroup means and SDs. The F tests and partial eta-squared values are omnibus method effects, not standardized GenAI-versus-control mean differences; all values are retained as printed and no effect sizes were computed (p. 8, Table 2 and Section 4.1). Elaboration has only a nonsignificant omnibus p-value threshold, with no printed pairwise test (p. 8, Section 4.1). The originality versus Unaided significance threshold comes from the single-star bracket in Figure 4; no exact pairwise p-value is supplied (p. 10). The support summary follows Section 4.2 (pp. 9-10); these self-reports are distinct from output-scored creativity (p. 7, Table 1 and Section 3.4). The full markdown was read through the final references; no appendix or supplement appears in that document. Figures 2, 4 and 5 were inspected directly from the PDF in memory.
